thread:
emma_support: Heads-up — customer ACMECorp opened an escalation. Since last night deploy they see 8–12x slower p95 on /v1/embeddings and ~1% of requests returning 400 errors saying dimension mismatch. Appears across multiple regions. Any quick triage steps?

own_sre: Can you paste a failing request + response (no secrets)? Also which model + alias they called?

emma_support: Pasting sanitized curl and the literal API response (removed API_KEY):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-emb-large-v2","input":["hello world"]}'
```
Response: `400 Bad Request`
```json
{"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: model expected 1536 but input vector size 512","request_id":"req_01G8XYZ","trace_id":"trace-0a1b2c3d"}
```
Headers on the response included `x-route: embeddings-prod-eu`, `x-latency-ms: 3120`.

owen_sre: OK good. Two things to check fast: 1) Did the model catalog swap aliases to a new model with different dim (sounds likely). 2) Check batching hook: if a client is sending precomputed vectors and we mistakenly treat as raw text, dims mismatch can happen.

liam_ml: Quick note — we rolled out `open-emb-large-v2` as default alias in yesterday's model onboarding (2026-03-14 22:10 UTC). It has 1536 dims. Previous default `open-emb-base` was 512. If some SDK users are still sending 512-sized precomputed vectors (they shouldn't for the text->embedding route, but some customers call our embeddings route with precomputed vectors), that would explain the error.

sofia_product: Are customers sending precomputed embeddings? ACME's note indicates they migrated a client service that preprocesses text into 512d vectors then passed them through our endpoint expecting a passthrough. They might have relied on the old model behavior.

emma_support: ACME provided sample logs showing their client did send a `vectors` field instead of `input`. They say it worked before.

own_sre: For the latency regression: can you pull per-request breakdown for one of the slow traces? I want tokenization -> routing -> queue -> inference -> postprocessing numbers.

emma_support: Attached trace id from their failing request: `trace-0a1b2c3d`. I grabbed a quick JSON from trace viewer:
```
trace_id: trace-0a1b2c3d
span: client.connect -> 25ms
span: routing.lookup -> 8ms
span: queue.wait -> 2400ms
span: batch.coalesce -> 35ms
span: kernel.infer -> 600ms
span: response.serialize -> 52ms
```

own_sre: Queue.wait is huge — 2.4s. That suggests batch scheduling/backpressure. Which batcher config is active on embeddings-prod-eu?

liam_ml: Post-deploy we changed the continuous-batcher target batch size from 8 -> 32 to improve throughput for large text workloads. That helps throughput but increases latency when traffic is bursty or per-request size is small. If customers send a lot of tiny requests the queue will hold to reach target batch size.

sofia_product: Can we add a dynamic policy: target batch size per-route or per-tenant? ACME is on shared tier and sensitive to p95.

own_sre: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Reduce target batch size for `embeddings` route in eu region back to 8. 2) Add a per-tenant override to route ACME to a lower batch-size pool or priority queue. 3) If dimension errors persist, provide a temporary model alias fallback `open-emb-base-legacy` that maps to the 512d model.

tim_billing: Note — if clients retry on 400 they might double-charge some operations; we should check billing logs for repeated retries in the last 6 hours and consider issuing a credit if we broke contract.

emma_support: Triage checklist I'm doing now:
- [x] Confirmed model alias change and dims (liam confirmed).
- [x] Got failing curl + response and trace id.
- [ ] Reproduce locally with small batch traffic.
- [ ] Rollback or add alias fallback if ACME needs immediate unblock.
- [ ] Reduce batcher target on eu route and monitor p95.
- [ ] Coordinate billing credit if retries/billing spikes detected.

owen_sre: Repro steps I used to simulate the queue wait locally (notes for oncall):
1) Start embeddings runner with `BATCH_TARGET=32` and small worker pool.
2) Fire 200 concurrent tiny requests (0.5–1KB payload) at ~200 RPS using wrk or k6.
3) Capture route traces and look at `batch.coalesce` and `queue.wait`.
Example k6:```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function() {
  http.post('https://local-runner/v1/embeddings', JSON.stringify({model:'open-emb-large-v2',input:['a']}), {headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}});
  sleep(0.01);
}```

own_sre: If you want a quick config change runbook: 
- In console -> Deployments -> embeddings-prod-eu -> runtime-config -> continuous_batcher -> set `target_batch_size: 8` and `max_wait_ms: 50` -> save -> rollout. Should drop queue.wait quickly.

liam_ml: For the dim mismatch resolution, options:
- Server-side: accept older 512d inputs by auto-detecting dim and routing to `open-emb-base` alias if present, but that's risky and can mask client bugs.
- Client-side: ask ACME to update their client to send raw text or use the correct model alias.
- Quick fallback: create `open-emb-legacy` alias mapped to old 512d model and document temporary compatibility.

sofia_product: Recommend quick fallback alias + batch size tweak as immediate remedies, plus a product ticket for per-tenant batching policies and a migration guide for model dim changes. I'll open a ticket and tag ACME for a scheduled migration.

tim_billing: I've flagged potential overbilling cases and will put a temporary hold on automated invoices for ACME until we confirm.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: change `continuous_batcher.target_batch_size` for `embeddings-prod-eu` -> 8 by owen_sre. RolloutID: r-2026-03-15-09.

own_sre: After the batch config change we should watch p95 over the next 30 minutes. Emma, can you ask ACME to run a quick smoke and paste a couple new trace ids?

emma_support: Will do. I'll also offer them the `open-emb-legacy` alias if they need it immediately and will escalate billing hold.

sofia_product: Followups for product backlog: add per-tenant batching, add a console alert when model alias dim changes, and an automated migration notifier for breaking model changes.

own_sre: Leaving notes for postmortem: root cause = model alias swap (512->1536) + batcher config change (8->32) -> together led to both dimension errors and higher p95 for tiny requests. Mitigation = alias fallback + batching config rollback + billing hold + customer comms.

emma_support: Marking this escalated -> CUSTOMER BLOCKING. Will update ACME and paste new traces once they run. :white_check_mark:
